principles.name: Use hook contact when pinch support is contradicted
principles.applicability: A narrow door handle is visible and the measured pad gap does not support the fitted handle width, or closure produces a near-zero gap without physical-contact evidence.
observable_failure_signals: The gripper gap collapses toward zero while the bar remains wider than the pads.
The grasp report says grasp_not_verified or near_closed_without_bar_width_support.
The part does not follow the hand in measured RGB-D motion.
conditional_actions: Open the gripper and inspect a fresh hook preview on the current handle.
Proceed only when the retaining feature and its back surface are observed and a robot-valid approach is available.
After motion, accept engagement only when current part-motion evidence supports it; otherwise reselect the contact or use another visible surface.
supporting_attempts: Attempt 6: pinch closures were unsupported; open-gripper hook pulls later produced measured door-follow motion.
Attempt 3: a hook attempt without a supported catch did not establish engagement.
principles.limits: The positive evidence came from one opening episode in this microwave scene. The door remained natively incomplete. A preview is not proof of hook engagement, and a retaining surface can become hidden as the panel moves.

principles.name: Reground handle and panel after every meaningful door motion
principles.applicability: A push, pull, grasped arc, or contact skill has changed the visible door angle or invalidated the current scene model.
observable_failure_signals: A previously selected region no longer overlays the handle.
The requested contact is reported outside the target patch or the retaining surface is unobserved.
RGB-D matching becomes inconsistent or the current motion estimate conflicts with the image.
conditional_actions: Use a fresh capture and fit the current handle and panel while retaining a hinge hypothesis only if it remains useful.
Inspect a second current view for hook support when the front view cannot show the retaining surface.
Do not reuse prior contact geometry or assume the part followed the robot; compare measured motion and the current image before continuing.
supporting_attempts: Attempt 5: contact and hinge discrepancies accumulated after repeated motion and required refreshed geometry.
Attempt 6: hook support varied by camera and door angle; fresh selection restored some engagements and exposed other failed selections.
principles.limits: Fresh geometry preserves the previous fixed-hinge and signed-direction assumptions; it does not independently verify them. This was tested on microwave-door scenes only.

principles.name: Keep task direction separate from joint sign
principles.applicability: The installed model has a signed axis, but opening or closing direction is not independently verified, or the task changes between episodes.
observable_failure_signals: The door moves opposite the visible goal relationship.
An image hint or tracker is unresolved while the model still labels one sign as open or close.
A motion produces movement but the native task boolean remains false.
conditional_actions: Make a bounded physical motion only from current robot-valid geometry, then inspect the changed door-cavity relationship and measured joint-axis motion.
Continue the same sign only when current evidence shows movement toward the requested state; otherwise update the direction hypothesis.
Use native task_success as the completion criterion, not a direction label, appearance alone, or robot motion.
supporting_attempts: Attempt 3: opening-direction assumptions were contradicted by observed outcomes.
Attempt 6: positive motion was supported as opening by measured and visible door movement, yet remained below native success.
Attempts 1 and 4: successful closing used scene-specific contact and direction choices.
principles.limits: The axis and direction evidence were not independently verified across scenes. This principle does not supply a universal world direction or opening threshold.

principles.name: Treat collision and motion predictions as evidence, not outcomes
principles.applicability: A contact preview reports an environmental overlap, or an executed skill returns false, unresolved, or partial progress.
observable_failure_signals: A plan is marked robot-valid while an advisory environment overlap is also reported.
The robot moves but RGB-D part motion is rejected or inconsistent.
The skill returns before native success, including after measurable partial motion.
conditional_actions: Inspect the reported prediction and contact overlay, then judge physical motion from the returned capture and RGB-D evidence.
If tracking is unresolved, compare fresh images and re-estimate geometry; do not invent attachment from hand motion.
After accepted partial progress, continue only with a current valid plan and sufficient attempt budget; check native success after every action.
supporting_attempts: Attempt 5: robot travel and rejected or inconsistent tracking did not reliably indicate door progress.
Attempt 6: advisory overlap did not itself prevent execution, while other valid plans failed to establish engagement; accepted RGB-D motion still did not guarantee native completion.
principles.limits: The contact predictions were incomplete and scene-specific. RGB-D evidence can fail or be occluded, and accepted rigid motion is not a native task certificate.
